inputs.text: ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.

fields.description: Fog warning: thick fog may cut visibility to zero at times across western regions of the UAE, from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Source: National Center for Meteorology.
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions
fields.instruction: Drive with extreme caution. Keep a safe distance and follow reduced speed limits in fog. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so none were excluded.
The 'Abu Dhabi' dateline is where the news story was filed, not a stated fog area, so it is not used as a location.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I chose severity Moderate and certainty Likely because NCM describes 'potential' fog, though possible zero visibility could justify Severe. NCM says 'several western regions' without naming them, so please confirm the operator's demo zone matches that area.

no_basis.concern: Severity 'Moderate' and certainty 'Likely' are not stated in the bulletin; the bulletin says 'potential fog formation' and 'expected' deterioration, so these values are a judgement by the drafter.
no_basis.searched_for: CAP severity and certainty definitions for fog warnings, and WMO impact-based guidance on severity and certainty levels. The clauses returned only describe US WEA or Canadian profile rules, not NCM fog thresholds.

payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin: same hazard (fog and reduced visibility), same area (western regions of the UAE), same times (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb), and the same visibility drop to zero at times. It names NCM as the source and includes no unverified reports. Severity (Moderate) and certainty (Likely) are not contradicted by the bulletin, and the clauses shown give no basis for changing them.

payload.summary: Within the issuing-authority mandate nothing is wrong. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with all areas and categories. The requested area (Western region demo zone, AUH-WEST, drawn for event uae-fog-2026-02-17) matches the alert area and codes. Status Actual with msgType Alert fits a real event on a live console. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach, and an initial Alert needs no references.

no_basis.concern: The texts state the hazard, area and time but give no explicit protective action (e.g. drive slowly, avoid travel); the first page may therefore carry no action.

no_basis.concern: TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page, which conflicts with the 3 and 6 page messages. It is a 'should' in a summary, and the handset spec TS FS 001 v2.0 sets no page limit and G6 is a recorded gap, so it is not raised again.
no_basis.searched_for: TDRA page limit for cell broadcast messages

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is 3 pages (GSM-7) and Arabic is 6 pages (UCS-2), both well under the 15-page maximum in 3GPP TS 23.041. Encodings fit the text: GSM-7 for English and UCS-2 for Arabic. Each language opens with the hazard (fog warning, visibility cut to zero) and its time window. Length beyond one page is already recorded as gap G6, so I do not object to it. The first-page action is not clearly present in either text, but no clause shown sets that requirement, so I record it as no-basis.

The Arabic was machine translated, so a named Arabic reader must still approve it.
